faq.q: Why should I say it out loud first?
faq.a: Saying it first helps you find the words before you write. Then your hand only has to write what you already said.

faq.q: How much should I write at once?
faq.a: Start with one sentence, then take a short break if you need it. Small steps add up to lots of writing.
asks: How many sentences at a time?

faq.q: How long should my breaks be?
faq.a: Short, like a stretch or a sip of water. Then come straight back for the next step.

faq.q: What if I forget my idea?
faq.a: Jot one word or draw a quick picture to remember it. You can also ask a grown-up to write your idea down while you talk.

faq.q: Can someone check my steps with me?
faq.a: Yes. A teacher or grown-up can make you a step card and tick each step as you finish it.
asks: Can I have a step card?

facts: Breaking a big task into small steps is a common way to make it feel easier.
